jobs.description:
Explore opportunities with At Home Hospice, a part of LHC Group, a leading post-acute care partner for hospitals, physicians and families nationwide. Find a home for your career here. Join us and embrace a culture of Caring. Connecting. Growing together.

As the Registered Nurse Case Manager, you will assume full nursing responsibility for the delivery of the Plan of Care for each hospice patient. Continuously evaluating personal and professional performance and making necessary changes to increase productivity and quality of care delivered. You'll also develop the patient's Plan of care in collaboration with other professionals and implement treatment strategies based on scientific nursing theory that promotes physical, psychosocial, emotional, and spiritual well-being. Familiar with the concepts and needs of patients/families who are facing death and dying.

Primary Responsibilities

Makes the initial nursing evaluation in determining eligibility for hospice services during visit within forty-eight (48) hours of referral
Identifies the patient's/family's physical, psychosocial, and environmental needs and re-assesses as needed, no less than every fifteen (15) days
Initiates and coordinates the plan of care
Documents problems, appropriate goals, interventions, and patient/family response to hospice care
Collaborates with the patient/family, attending physician and other members of the IDG in providing patient and family care daily
Instructs and supervises the patient/family in self-care techniques when appropriate
Maintains accurate and relevant clinical notes regarding the patient's condition
Ability to function in any home situation regardless of age, race, creed, color, sex, disability, or financial condition of the client

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

Required Qualifications

Current and unrestricted RN licensure in the state of practice
Current driver's license, valid vehicle insurance, and access to a dependable vehicle, or public transportation

Preferred Qualifications

1+ years of clinical experience
Current CPR certification or ability to complete within 90 days of hire

Pay is based on several factors including but not limited to local labor markets, education, work experience, certifications, etc. In addition to your salary, we offer benefits such as, a comprehensive benefits package, incentive and recognition programs, equity stock purchase and 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Do you want to make a real difference to adults with mental health and substance misuse difficulties? If so, join us!

At East Sussex County Council, we have a commitment to empowering adults. Our aim is to maximise their independence and help them play a full part in the decisions that affect them. Joining our Adult Social Care Mental Health West Team, based in Eastbourne is a chance to change your world and theirs. You will be supported by a team that cares for you, just as much as it cares for our community.

You will have a varied caseload, providing social care for adults with mental health and substance misuse issues. This includes investigating safeguarding concerns, carrying out statutory assessments, commissioning support and presenting your reports to panels or in court. You will also work with partner agencies, carers, and families to build networks of support that can help people maintain their independence. As part of your responsibilities, you will train as an Approved Mental Health Professional (AMHP) and take part in AMHP rotas when required. With an increased demand for our services, we have to adapt and be creative, so there are plenty of opportunities to learn and innovate.

The role involves working with adults between the ages of 18 – 70 with severe and enduring mental needs and adults over the age of 18 with no upper age limit with substance misuse needs.

Hybrid working arrangements are applicable to the role this includes elements of office-based working, client visits and working from home. You will need to demonstrate you can meet the travel requirements of the role.

Has Social work qualifications and registered with the professional regulatory body.

Social Worker

High Peak South Adult Social Work Team, Buxton
Full Time - 37 hours per week

The High Peak South Adult Social Work Team, based in Buxton, is seeking to recruit an experienced and enthusiastic Social Worker to join our friendly, supportive community-based team of Social Workers, Social Care Practitioners and Community Connectors.

This is a full-time position working 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday.

Our team operates across the High Peak area of Derbyshire using a flexible and largely agile approach to working. We utilise link worker and champion roles to support the delivery of Care Act 2014 assessments and reviews through both face-to-face and telephone-based interventions.

As a Social Worker within our team, you will be expected to demonstrate a high level of autonomy, professional accountability and effective case management. Timely recording of interventions and the ability to progress work efficiently are essential.

You will work closely with a range of partner agencies including Health services, the Police, Housing providers and private, voluntary and independent sector organisations. Building positive professional relationships, identifying opportunities for signposting and supporting carers are key elements of the role. We are committed to promoting independence, wellbeing and person-centred, strengths-based outcomes for the people we support.

What We're Looking For

The successful candidate will be able to:

Manage a complex caseload effectively and safely.
Be registered with Social Work England
Complete assessments and reviews in line with the Care Act 2014.
Demonstrate sound professional judgement and decision-making.
Work collaboratively with partner organisations and community resources.
Promote a safety of service users through the use of Safeguarding processes and protocols
Promote independence and strengths-based practice.
Meet statutory duties in an accountable and cost-effective manner.
Maintain accurate and timely case recording.

The role also includes participation in Duty cover. You will need to respond effectively to changing circumstances, triage incoming work and assess urgency to ensure adults and carers receive the appropriate level of support.

Desirable Experience

While not essential, experience in the following areas would be advantageous:

Leading Section 42 Safeguarding enquiries.
Chairing multi-agency meetings, including Multi-Agency Adult Risk Management (MARM) meetings.
Completing Mental Capacity Act 2005 assessments.
Facilitating Best Interest meetings.
Court of Protection Deprivation of Liberty (COP DoL) applications.
Court work.

A comprehensive induction programme, ongoing support and training will be provided to help develop skills in these areas.

Why Join Derbyshire County Council?

Derbyshire County Council is a fantastic place to work, offering supportive teams, opportunities for professional development and a range of employee benefits.

You will receive:

Regular monthly supervision as a minimum.
Informal support from colleagues, peers and managers.
Access to training and development opportunities.
A culture that promotes reflection, learning and knowledge sharing.
Opportunities to undertake champion and specialist roles within the team.

Employee Benefits

Employees have access to a wide range of benefits including:

Local Government Pension Scheme.
25 or 27 days annual leave per year, rising to 30 or 32 days after five years' continuous service (grade dependent), plus bank holidays.
Training and development opportunities.
Paid travel expenses where required.
Cycle to Work Scheme and Smarter Travel initiatives.
Supportive management and team environment.
Occupational Health services, including free eye tests, physiotherapy and counselling.
Derbyshire Rewards, offering hundreds of discounts and cashback opportunities.

Only candidates who are registered, or eligible to register, with Social Work England
will be shortlisted.

For an informal discussion about the role, please contact:

Karen Wright
Service Manager, High Peak South karen.wright@derbyshire.gov.uk

Provisional interviews are expected to take place in October 2026.

Lead a small team that keeps prison operations running every day.
Plan rosters, solve complex staffing issues and support a busy workplace.

Ongoing, full-time role earning $81,496 - $98,955 per year, plus super.

plan and maintain staff rosters up to six weeks ahead while meeting operational needs and workplace requirements.
monitor roster data, timesheets and attendance records to keep information accurate and resolve complex issues.

clear communication skills with a flexible and inclusive approach to working with others.
